# Runtime 298→410 alpha-discrepancy reconciliation

Generated: 2026-08-20T16:31:45.736Z

Reference: [original discrepancy analysis](https://gist.github.com/UnArbosFour/0ea73fe2a78b209f69e3080cef7356e2)

## Verdict

**No. The release-298-through-410 mechanism does not explain today's discrepancy.** Its predicted permanent mainnet accrual is 0.000000000 α, while the current signed aggregate is +389,557.175298267 α.

The old undercount is reachable only in the stable (mechanism 0) branch of `swap_tao_for_alpha`. Mainnet's 128 alpha subnets were all mechanism 1 at the runtime-298 introduction boundary and immediately before the deployed 410-era refactor (mainnet spec 411). Archived state at both edges of the 2,177,293-block window reports mechanism 1 for all 128 alpha subnets (256 values checked). This is paired with the runtime-298 source invariant: subnet registration rejects any `mechid` other than 1, both registration dispatches pass 1, and no live runtime path changes an active alpha subnet to mechanism 0. Therefore every alpha-subnet generation in this window follows the dynamic branch.

For mechanism 1, the buy swap first adds the bought alpha to `SubnetAlphaOut`; the release-298 subsidy code then subtracts that same amount. The net effect of the protocol buy is zero, while the participant emission is added normally. There is therefore no permanent `SubnetAlphaOut` undercount on the historical mainnet path.

## Why the earlier clone result was a false positive

The previous adjacent-block replay's formula-native discrepancy movement was at most 0.000000002 α (2 rao). It became +12.963919817 α only after every `PendingAlphaSwapped` increment was reclassified as unsold alpha. That field has mixed semantics: on the ordinary branch it records alpha already sold for root TAO and must not be counted as a pending alpha claim. The replay did not establish that the subsidy branch executed; its near-zero native movement is the valid control.

## Counter recommendation

Do not adjust `SubnetAlphaOut`, `AlphaBurned`, or `SubnetProtocolAlpha` based on this hypothesis. The supported correction amount is zero. Mechanically, if a real release-298 stable-branch undercount had accrued, the semantic repair would be `SubnetAlphaOut += undercount`: the alpha was neither burned nor protocol-owned. But that branch did not run for mainnet alpha subnets, so applying such a correction now would create a new negative discrepancy. Decreasing burned or protocol alpha would also be unsupported without independent evidence that either counter is overstated.
